subject: Provenance and retention for LLM-derived outputs — DPO follow-up
messages:
From: Elena Morales <dpo@datashield.inc>
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Cc: legal@datashield.inc
Date: Fri, 1 Oct 2027 15:12:00 -0400
Subject: LLM outputs / training provenance - request

Hi Karthik,

Thanks again for the demo last week. As part of our procurement & DPIA review, our Data Protection team needs a concise package to confirm how Redwood handles customer-provided prompts and generated outputs. Specifically: 

1) Training: Are customer prompts or generated responses ever incorporated into models used in production or downstream research? If yes, please describe de-identification or consent controls.
2) Derivative provenance: For outputs that may be derived (summaries, transformed content), do you maintain provenance metadata that ties outputs back to input artifacts? If so, what fields are retained and how long?
3) Opt-out: We need the opt-out workflow and SLA for excluding a tenant's data from training or derivative datasets.
4) Retention: Clarify prompt/response retention periods for hosted API and Dedicated deployments, including any ephemeral caching behavior.
5) Evidence: Can you provide a sample audit log (anonymized) showing a deletion/opt-out event and confirmation that it propagated to training/derivative pipelines?

We'd appreciate an initial response within 3 business days; final attestation and any formal language we can include in our DPA within 10 business days. If there are standard CAIQ/SIG artifacts that map to the items above, please point us to them.

Best,
Elena
DPO, DataShield Inc.

---
DataShield Inc. (external)

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
To: Elena Morales <dpo@datashield.inc>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 1 Oct 2027 17:05:00 -0400
Subject: Re: LLM outputs / training provenance - request

Thanks Elena — appreciate the clear list. Looping in Marissa (account lead) and Ben (security/compliance) so we can coordinate a short package. High-level answers up front to speed triage:

- Training: By default, customer inputs are not used to train our public model catalog. We offer an opt-in training flow for specific enterprise customers; otherwise we provide a strict no-train default for hosted accounts.
- Derivative provenance: We persist request metadata (request id, timestamp, model version, tenant id when applicable) and link generated outputs to the request id. We do not store model internal gradients or training checkpoints as part of request storage.
- Opt-out: We have a documented no-train opt-out that can be set at tenant level; when applied, it triggers removal of recent prompt/response records from short-term caches and flags data for exclusion from longer-term dataset ingestion pipelines.
- Retention: Hosted API default: 30 days for prompt/response artifacts (used for caching/diagnostics), Dedicated: configurable by contract; Private deployments: customer-managed.

We'll prepare an anonymized sample audit log and a short write-up addressing the provenance fields and propagation proof. Ben, could you confirm the propagation timeline and whether we can include a signed attestation? Marissa, I'll also draft a suggested DPA paragraph for Elena's legal team.

Thanks,
Karthik
Director, Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

Attachment: initial-request-checklist.txt (stub)

From: Elena Morales <dpo@datashield.inc>
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 4 Oct 2027 09:03:00 +0200
Subject: Re: LLM outputs / training provenance - request

Karthik — thanks for the quick summary. Couple of clarifications that would be helpful for our privacy team: 

- When you say "persist request metadata", can you enumerate exact fields included in the request id record (e.g., full prompt text, client IP, tenant id, model hash, derived-output id)? Which of those are retained in audit logs vs short-term caches?
- For the opt-out propagation: what is the SLA (hours/days) between flagging opt-out and removal from every downstream system (including ingestion queues)?
- For the anonymized audit log, please ensure timestamps and IDs are obfuscated but the event flow (opt-out request -> deletion job -> pipeline exclusion) is clearly visible.

If you can provide a single zipped packet (CAIQ mappings, a short attestation paragraph, the sample log, and a DPA-friendly clause we can drop in), that would be ideal.

Elena

---
DataShield Inc. (external)

From: ben_carter@redwood.com
To: Elena Morales <dpo@datashield.inc>, karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Sat, 2 Oct 2027 10:46:00 -0400
Subject: Re: LLM outputs / training provenance - request

Hi Elena — Ben from Security/Privacy here. Apologies for the slight overlap on dates (we prioritised prepping the packet). Attached is a zipped packet and a short attestation. Summary highlights below and links to artifacts: 

1) Fields retained: request_id (opaque UUID), tenant_id (hashed for multi-tenant hosted), model_version, timestamp, response_id, processing_node_id, ephemeral_cache_key. We do NOT retain client IPs in production audit exports; IPs are redacted in logs by default. Full prompt text is retained for hosted accounts up to 30 days for diagnostic/cache purposes; when a tenant opts out, prompt/response text associated with that tenant is removed from both cache and the 30-day store and flagged in the ingestion ledger.

2) Opt-out SLA: For hosted API accounts, opt-out propagation is completed within 48 hours in >99% of cases (typical observed median ~6 hours). The packet includes a sample audit run for an opt-out on 2027-09-18 showing the job timeline.

3) Training pipelines: We have an enterprise-only opt-in training feed; data marked as no-train is excluded from the ingestion bucket and a signed exclusion marker is stored. We include a candidate CAIQ mapping (controls SC-1, SC-3, PL-2 mapped to our retention/opt-out behavior) and an attestation paragraph you can paste into your DPA.

Attachments (in zip):
- redwood-llm-retention-summary.pdf (summary + CAIQ mapping)
- sample-audit-log-2027-09.csv (anonymized row sequence)
- redwood-no-train-attestation.txt
- suggested-dpa-llm-clause.txt

If you'd like a short call to walk through the packet, Marissa and I are available next week. Happy to tighten timelines if DataShield needs a formal SLA amendment.

Regards,
Ben Carter
Head of Security & Compliance
Redwood Inference

---
Attachments: redwood-llm-retention-summary.pdf (PDF), sample-audit-log-2027-09.csv (CSV), redwood-no-train-attestation.txt (TXT), suggested-dpa-llm-clause.txt (TXT)
